nodes.outcome: Explain why passengers lean outward when a vehicle takes a sharp curved turn using inertia of direction.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Explain Use of Mudguards via Inertia
nodes.outcome: Explain why mud flying tangentially from rotating vehicle tires requires mudguards based on inertia of direction.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Relate Mass as the Measure of Inertia
nodes.outcome: State that mass is the quantitative measure of an object's inertia.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Compare Inertia of Everyday Objects
nodes.outcome: Compare the inertia of pairs of objects (e.g., a football vs a stone, a bicycle vs a train, a 5-rupee coin vs a 1-rupee coin) based on their masses.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Define Linear Momentum
nodes.outcome: Define linear momentum of an object as the product of its mass and its velocity (p = mv).

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: State the SI Unit of Momentum
nodes.outcome: State and derive the SI unit of momentum as kilogram meter per second (kg m/s).

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Identify Momentum as a Vector
nodes.outcome: Identify that momentum has both magnitude and direction, and that its direction is identical to the direction of velocity.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Calculate Momentum from Mass and Velocity
nodes.outcome: Calculate the linear momentum of a moving body given its mass and velocity.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Compare Momentum Across Scales
nodes.outcome: Compare the momentum and impact of a small mass moving at high speed (like a bullet) versus a massive body moving at low speed (like a rolling truck).

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Calculate Change in Momentum
nodes.outcome: Calculate the change in momentum (Δp = m*v - m*u) for an object undergoing acceleration along a straight path.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: State Newton's Second Law of Motion
nodes.outcome: State Newton's Second Law of Motion: the rate of change of momentum of an object is proportional to the applied unbalanced force and takes place in the direction of the force.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Derive Mathematical Formula F = ma
nodes.outcome: Derive the formula F = k * m(v - u)/t = ma from the statement of Newton's Second Law of Motion.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Define the SI Unit of Force (Newton)
nodes.outcome: Define 1 Newton (N) as the amount of force that produces an acceleration of 1 m/s² on a body of mass 1 kg, establishing k = 1.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Calculate Force Given Mass and Acceleration
nodes.outcome: Calculate the magnitude of force required to produce a specific acceleration on a known mass.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Calculate Acceleration from Force and Mass
nodes.outcome: Calculate the acceleration produced in a body given the applied force and its mass.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Solve Force Problems Combining Equations of Motion
nodes.outcome: Solve multi-step numerical problems requiring the calculation of force using equations of motion (v = u + at, s = ut + 0.5at², v² - u² = 2as) to determine acceleration.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Derive First Law from Second Law
nodes.outcome: Show mathematically that when F = 0 in F = m(v - u)/t, v = u, thereby deriving the First Law from the Second Law.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Relate Impact Force Inversely to Time of Contact
nodes.outcome: Explain why increasing the time over which momentum changes reduces the impact force (F = Δp / Δt).

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Explain Cricket Fielder Pulling Hands Back
nodes.outcome: Explain why a cricket fielder pulls their hands backward while catching a fast-moving ball using the relationship F = Δp / Δt.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Explain Sand Cushion in High Jump
nodes.outcome: Explain why high jumpers or long jumpers land on a cushioned bed or sand pit to prevent injury using the Second Law.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Explain Breaking Tiles in Karate
nodes.outcome: Explain how a karate player breaks a pile of tiles or ice slab with a swift blow by minimizing contact time.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: State Newton's Third Law of Motion
nodes.outcome: State Newton's Third Law of Motion: to every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Recognize Simultaneity of Action and Reaction
nodes.outcome: Identify that action and reaction forces occur simultaneously and neither force precedes the other.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Explain Action-Reaction Act on Different Bodies
nodes.outcome: Explain why action and reaction forces do not cancel each other out by emphasizing that they always act on two different bodies.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Demonstrate Action-Reaction with Spring Balances
nodes.outcome: Describe the connected spring balances experiment showing that both balances show identical readings in opposite directions.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Explain Walking Mechanism via Third Law
nodes.outcome: Identify the action (feet pushing the ground backward) and reaction (ground pushing feet forward) forces during walking.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Explain Gun Recoil via Action and Reaction
nodes.outcome: Identify the action force on the bullet and the reaction force on the gun causing it to recoil backward.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Compare Gun and Bullet Accelerations
nodes.outcome: Explain why the gun's recoil acceleration is much smaller than the bullet's acceleration despite experiencing equal forces (a = F/m).

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Explain Sailor Jumping from Boat
nodes.outcome: Explain why a rowboat moves backward into water when a sailor jumps forward onto the shore.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Explain Rocket Propulsion via Third Law
nodes.outcome: Explain rocket propulsion in terms of action (downward expulsion of exhaust gases) and reaction (upward thrust on rocket).

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Explain Deflating Balloon Motion
nodes.outcome: Explain the movement of a straw-guided deflating balloon as an illustration of action-reaction.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: State the Law of Conservation of Momentum
nodes.outcome: State the Law of Conservation of Momentum: the total momentum of an isolated system of colliding bodies remains constant provided no external unbalanced force acts on it.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Derive Conservation of Momentum for Two Bodies
nodes.outcome: Derive m₁u₁ + m₂u₂ = m₁v₁ + m₂v₂ for two colliding balls using Newton's Second and Third Laws (F₁₂ = -F₂₁).

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Calculate Gun Recoil Velocity
nodes.outcome: Calculate the recoil velocity of a firearm after shooting a projectile using conservation of linear momentum.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Calculate Post-Collision Velocity
nodes.outcome: Calculate the common velocity or individual final velocity of two bodies after collision using the conservation of momentum formula.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Solve Person-Cart Jumping Momentum Problems
nodes.outcome: Solve numerical problems where a person jumps onto or off a rolling cart using momentum conservation.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Synthesize and Compare Newton's Three Laws
nodes.outcome: Compare and distinguish the roles of Newton's First, Second, and Third Laws in defining, measuring, and characterizing the nature of forces.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Evaluate Complex Force and Motion Scenarios
nodes.outcome: Predict and analyze the motion of interconnected systems (e.g., connected blocks, rocket flight with mass ejection) by synthesizing Newton's three laws and conservation principles.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Colloquial vs Scientific Work
nodes.outcome: Contrast everyday uses of the word 'work' with its precise scientific definition

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Conditions for Work Done
nodes.outcome: State the two essential conditions required for work to be done on an object

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Identify Work in Scenarios
nodes.outcome: Identify whether work is done in everyday scenarios such as pushing a stationary wall, reading, or pulling a trolley

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Zero Work for Stationary Load
nodes.outcome: Explain why holding a heavy load stationary on one's head results in zero work done despite physical fatigue

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Formula for Work Done
nodes.outcome: State the mathematical expression for work done when a constant force acts in the direction of displacement: W = F * s

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: SI Unit of Work
nodes.outcome: State the SI unit of work as Joule (J) and define 1 Joule of work

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Calculate Work (Same Direction)
nodes.outcome: Calculate the work done when force and displacement are in the same direction

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Define Positive Work
nodes.outcome: Define positive work done as occurring when the applied force and displacement are in the same direction

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Define Negative Work
nodes.outcome: Define negative work done as occurring when the applied force acts opposite to the direction of displacement: W = -F * s

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Work Done by Friction
nodes.outcome: Explain why work done by the force of friction on a moving object is negative

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Work Done by Perpendicular Force
nodes.outcome: Explain why the work done is zero when the applied force is perpendicular to the displacement

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Work Done in Circular Orbit
nodes.outcome: Apply the perpendicular force condition to deduce that gravitational force does zero work on a planet moving in a circular orbit

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Calculate Negative Work
nodes.outcome: Calculate the work done by a retarding or opposing force given force and displacement values

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Classify Sign of Work Done
nodes.outcome: Classify work done as positive, negative, or zero for various physical forces acting on a body

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Define Energy
nodes.outcome: Define energy as the capacity or capability of an object to do work

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: SI Unit of Energy
nodes.outcome: State that the SI unit of energy is the Joule (J) and define 1 kiloJoule (kJ)

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Energy Transfer Mechanism
nodes.outcome: Describe how an object possessing energy loses energy when doing work on another object which gains energy

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: List Forms of Energy
nodes.outcome: List major forms of energy including kinetic, potential, heat, chemical, light, sound, and electrical energy

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Define Mechanical Energy
nodes.outcome: Define mechanical energy as the sum total of the kinetic energy and potential energy of a body

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Define Kinetic Energy
nodes.outcome: Define kinetic energy as the energy possessed by an object due to its state of motion

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Examples of Kinetic Energy
nodes.outcome: Identify everyday examples of kinetic energy such as a falling coconut, a speeding car, a rolling stone, and blowing wind

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Factors Affecting Kinetic Energy
nodes.outcome: State that the kinetic energy of an object increases with its mass and with the square of its speed

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Derive Kinetic Energy Formula
nodes.outcome: Derive the formula E_k = 1/2 * m * v^2 using the third equation of motion (v^2 - u^2 = 2as) and W = F * s

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Work-Energy Theorem
nodes.outcome: Demonstrate that the work done by a net force on a moving object equals the change in its kinetic energy: W = 1/2 * m * v^2 - 1/2 * m * u^2

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Calculate Kinetic Energy
nodes.outcome: Calculate the kinetic energy of an object given its mass and velocity

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Calculate Work to Change Speed
nodes.outcome: Calculate the work required to accelerate or decelerate a vehicle from an initial velocity u to a final velocity v

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Proportionality of Kinetic Energy
nodes.outcome: Predict the factor by which kinetic energy changes when the velocity of an object is doubled or tripled

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Relate Kinetic Energy and Momentum
nodes.outcome: Relate kinetic energy to linear momentum using the formula E_k = p^2 / (2m)

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Define Potential Energy
nodes.outcome: Define potential energy as the energy stored in an object due to its position or change in configuration

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Elastic Potential Energy
nodes.outcome: Explain how work done in stretching or compressing an elastic body (like a spring or rubber band) is stored as elastic potential energy

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Stretched Bow Energy Transfer
nodes.outcome: Explain the release of an arrow from a stretched bow in terms of work done to deform the bow, storage of elastic potential energy, and conversion to kinetic energy

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Winding Key of a Toy Car
nodes.outcome: Describe the energy transformations that occur when winding the spring of a toy car and releasing it

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Define Gravitational PE
nodes.outcome: Define gravitational potential energy as the work done in raising an object from the ground to a certain height against gravity

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Derive Gravitational PE Formula
nodes.outcome: Derive the formula E_p = mgh for an object of mass m raised to a vertical height h against constant acceleration due to gravity g

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Calculate Gravitational PE
nodes.outcome: Calculate the gravitational potential energy of an object given its mass, height, and acceleration due to gravity

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Calculate Height from PE
nodes.outcome: Calculate the height to which an object of known mass is raised given its gravitational potential energy

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Path Independence of Gravitational PE
nodes.outcome: Explain why the gravitational potential energy of an object depends only on its initial and final vertical positions and not on the path taken

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Compare Work Along Different Paths
nodes.outcome: Compare the work done against gravity when lifting an object vertically versus moving it up an inclined ramp to the same vertical height

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Reference Level for Potential Energy
nodes.outcome: Explain how the choice of zero-level reference point affects the numerical value of potential energy without altering physical outcomes

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Concept of Energy Transformation
nodes.outcome: Define energy transformation as the process of changing energy from one form to another

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Energy Conversion in Electric Bulb
nodes.outcome: Describe the transformation of electrical energy into light and thermal energy in an electric bulb

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Energy Conversion in Photosynthesis
nodes.outcome: State the conversion of solar (light) energy into chemical energy during photosynthesis in green plants

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Energy Conversion in Thermal Power Plant
nodes.outcome: Trace the sequence of energy transformations from chemical energy of fuel to heat, kinetic energy of steam, and electrical energy in a power station

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Conversions in Household Appliances
nodes.outcome: Identify the primary energy conversions in household devices including electric motors, heaters, electric irons, and loudspeakers

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Energy Interconversion in Simple Pendulum
nodes.outcome: Trace the continuous interconversion between kinetic and potential energy as an oscillating pendulum bob moves between its mean and extreme positions

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Pendulum Damping and Energy Dissipation
nodes.outcome: Explain why an oscillating pendulum eventually comes to rest by accounting for mechanical energy lost as heat and sound due to air resistance

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Law of Conservation of Energy
nodes.outcome: State the Law of Conservation of Energy: energy can neither be created nor destroyed, only transformed from one form to another

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Constancy of Total Energy
nodes.outcome: State that the total energy of an isolated system remains constant before and after any transformation

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Qualitative Free Fall Energy Transition
nodes.outcome: Describe qualitatively how potential energy decreases while kinetic energy increases as an object falls freely from rest

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Derive Conservation in Free Fall
nodes.outcome: Prove mathematically that the mechanical energy (mgh + 1/2 * m * v^2) remains constant at the top, midway, and bottom points of a freely falling body

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Calculate Impact Velocity from Energy

nodes.outcome: Identify crop quality parameters tailored to specific crops, such as baking quality in wheat, protein quality in pulses, and oil quality in oilseeds

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Biotic and Abiotic Resistance Breeding
nodes.outcome: Distinguish between biotic stresses (diseases, insects, nematodes) and abiotic stresses (drought, salinity, heat, cold, frost) that reduce crop yield

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Shorter Maturity Duration Benefits
nodes.outcome: Explain the agronomic and economic benefits of reducing crop maturity duration, including multi-cropping and cost reduction

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Wider Adaptability in Crop Varieties
nodes.outcome: Explain how developing varieties with wider adaptability stabilizes crop production across varying climatic zones

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Desirable Agronomic Characteristics
nodes.outcome: Identify desirable agronomic characteristics for specific crops, such as profuse branching and tallness for fodder crops, and dwarfness for cereals

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Sixteen Essential Plant Nutrients by Source
nodes.outcome: List the 16 essential plant nutrients categorized by their sources: air (carbon, oxygen), water (hydrogen, oxygen), and soil (13 mineral nutrients)

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Macronutrients vs Micronutrients
nodes.outcome: Differentiate between macronutrients (required in large quantities: N, P, K, Ca, Mg, S) and micronutrients (required in small quantities: Fe, Mn, B, Zn, Cu, Mo, Cl)

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Effects of Nutrient Deficiencies
nodes.outcome: Explain how nutrient deficiencies affect physiological processes in plants, including growth, reproduction, and disease susceptibility

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Manure and Soil Health
nodes.outcome: Explain how manure enriches soil with organic matter and small quantities of nutrients, thereby improving soil structure, aeration, and water-holding capacity

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Composting vs Vermicomposting
nodes.outcome: Distinguish between compost prepared by decomposition in pits and vermicompost prepared using earthworms to hasten the decomposition process

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Green Manure Preparation and Role
nodes.outcome: Describe how growing and mulching green plants like sunn hemp or guar into the soil provides green manure enriched in nitrogen and phosphorus

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Chemical Fertilizers Composition and Role
nodes.outcome: Identify chemical fertilizers as commercially produced plant nutrients supplying nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium (NPK) for high vegetative growth

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Compare Manure and Fertilizers
nodes.outcome: Distinguish between manure and fertilizers based on composition, nutrient specificity, organic matter content, and long-term soil fertility effects

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Hazards of Excessive Fertilizer Use
nodes.outcome: Explain the ecological and soil hazards of excessive chemical fertilizer use, including destruction of soil micro-organisms and water pollution via runoff

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Principles of Organic Farming
nodes.outcome: Explain the core practices of organic farming, including zero or minimal use of chemical fertilizers/pesticides, use of bio-fertilizers, bio-pesticides, and crop rotation

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Need and Importance of Irrigation
nodes.outcome: Explain why timely irrigation is crucial for crop success in India due to spatial and temporal erratic rainfall patterns

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Major Irrigation Systems in India
nodes.outcome: Describe the main irrigation systems: dug wells, tube wells, canal systems, river lift systems, and tanks

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Rainwater Harvesting and Watershed Management
nodes.outcome: Explain how rainwater harvesting and check-dams in watershed management recharge groundwater tables and reduce soil erosion

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Mixed Cropping Concept and Examples
nodes.outcome: Define mixed cropping as growing two or more crops simultaneously on the same piece of land (e.g., wheat + gram) to reduce risk of total crop failure

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Intercropping System and Pattern
nodes.outcome: Describe intercropping as growing two or more crops simultaneously in a definite row pattern (e.g., soyabean + maize) to maximize nutrient utilization

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Crop Rotation Principle and Criteria
nodes.outcome: Explain the practice of crop rotation (growing different crops on a piece of land in a pre-planned succession) based on moisture availability and duration

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Weeds Definition and Examples
nodes.outcome: Define weeds as unwanted plants in cultivated fields and identify common examples like Xanthium (gokhroo), Parthenium (gajar ghas), and Cyperus rotundus (motha)

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Harmful Effects of Weeds on Crops
nodes.outcome: Explain how weeds compete with crops for food, space, and light, thereby severely reducing crop growth and yield

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Methods of Weed Control
nodes.outcome: Compare weed control methods including mechanical removal, use of chemical weedicides, and preventive practices like proper seed bed preparation and timely sowing

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Modes of Insect Pest Attacks
nodes.outcome: Classify insect pest attacks into three modes: cutting roots/stems/leaves, sucking cell sap, and boring into stems and fruits

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Plant Diseases and Transmission
nodes.outcome: Identify bacteria, fungi, and viruses as plant pathogens transmitted via soil, water, and air

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Pesticide Use and Environmental Hazards
nodes.outcome: Describe the use of pesticides (herbicides, insecticides, fungicides) and state the health and environmental risks of their indiscriminate use

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Factors Causing Storage Losses of Food Grains
nodes.outcome: Classify factors responsible for grain storage losses into biotic factors (insects, rodents, fungi, mites, bacteria) and abiotic factors (inappropriate moisture and temperatures)

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Consequences of Improper Grain Storage
nodes.outcome: List the consequences of improper grain storage, including weight loss, degradation in quality, poor germinability, and discoloration leading to poor marketability

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Preventive and Control Measures for Storage
nodes.outcome: Describe safe storage practices including strict cleaning, drying in sunlight then shade, and chemical fumigation to kill pests

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Definition of Animal Husbandry
nodes.outcome: Define animal husbandry as the scientific management of livestock including feeding, breeding, housing, and disease control

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Scientific Names of Indian Cattle and Buffalo
nodes.outcome: State Bos indicus as the scientific name for cow and Bos bubalis for buffalo

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Milch vs Draught Cattle
nodes.outcome: Distinguish between milch animals (dairy females reared for milk) and draught animals (males used for farm labor like tilling, carting, and irrigation)

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Lactation Period in Cattle
nodes.outcome: Define the lactation period as the duration of milk production following the birth of a calf and relate it to total milk yield

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Crossbreeding Exotic and Indigenous Cattle
nodes.outcome: Explain why exotic breeds (Jersey, Brown Swiss for long lactation periods) are crossbred with local breeds (Red Sindhi, Sahiwal for high disease resistance)

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Cattle Shelter and Grooming Requirements
nodes.outcome: Describe shelter and hygiene requirements for cattle, including well-ventilated roofed sheds, sloping dry floors, and regular brushing to remove dirt and loose hair

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Roughage and Concentrates in Cattle Feed
nodes.outcome: Distinguish between roughage (largely fiber) and concentrates (low fiber, high protein and nutrient levels) in dairy animal nutrition

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Cattle Parasites and Infectious Diseases
nodes.outcome: Differentiate between external parasites (causing skin diseases) and internal parasites (worms affecting stomach/intestines, flukes damaging liver), and state the importance of vaccination against viral and bacterial diseases

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Aims of Poultry Farming
nodes.outcome: State the primary aims of poultry farming as raising domestic fowls for egg production and chicken meat

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Crossbreeding Goals in Poultry
nodes.outcome: List breeding goals for crossbreeding indigenous (e.g., Aseel) and exotic (e.g., Leghorn) poultry breeds, including number/quality of chicks, dwarf broilers, high temperature tolerance, and low maintenance

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Layers vs Broilers
nodes.outcome: Distinguish between layers (egg-producing birds raised to adulthood) and broilers (meat-producing birds fed for rapid growth and marketed at 6 to 8 weeks)

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Nutritional Needs of Broilers vs Layers
nodes.outcome: Compare the daily food rations of broilers (protein-rich with adequate fats and high vitamins A and K) and egg layers

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Poultry Disease Prevention and Sanitation
nodes.outcome: Identify causes of poultry diseases (viruses, bacteria, fungi, parasites, nutritional deficiencies) and list preventive measures including cleaning, disinfection, and vaccination

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Capture Fishery vs Culture Fishery
nodes.outcome: Distinguish between capture fishery (obtaining fish from natural water bodies) and culture fishery (farming fish in controlled water enclosures)

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Marine Fisheries Resources and Methods
nodes.outcome: Identify popular marine fish varieties (pomphret, mackerel, tuna, sardines, Bombay duck) and explain the use of echo-sounders and satellites to locate large fish shoals

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Mariculture and High Economic Value Species
nodes.outcome: Define mariculture and list cultivated marine organisms including finned fishes (mullets, bhetki, pearl spots), shellfish (prawns, mussels, oysters), and seaweeds

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Inland Fisheries and Brackish Water
nodes.outcome: Classify inland water resources into fresh water systems (canals, ponds, rivers, reservoirs) and brackish water habitats (estuaries, lagoons)

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Principles of Composite Fish Culture
nodes.outcome: Explain the principle of composite fish culture using 5-6 selected species with non-competing food habits to maximize food utilization across all pond zones

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Species Selection in Composite Fish Culture
nodes.outcome: Identify feeding zones and food habits of species in composite fish culture: Catla (surface feeder), Rohu (middle zone feeder), Mrigal and Common Carp (bottom feeders), and Grass Carp (feeds on weeds)

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Hormonal Stimulation in Fish Breeding
nodes.outcome: Explain how hormonal stimulation overcomes the major problem of poor quality fish seed availability during monsoons

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Apiculture Products and Benefits
nodes.outcome: Define apiculture (bee-keeping) and identify honey and beeswax as its valuable commercial products

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Honeybee Species Used in Apiculture
nodes.outcome: Name indigenous bee species (Apis cerana indica, Apis dorsata, Apis florae) and the exotic Italian bee (Apis mellifera)

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Desirable Traits of the Italian Bee
nodes.outcome: List the commercial advantages of Apis mellifera: high honey collection capacity, less stinging, staying in hives for longer periods, and rapid breeding

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Pasturage and Honey Quality
nodes.outcome: Explain how pasturage (the flowers available to bees for nectar and pollen collection) determines the quantity, quality, and taste of honey
